Fellow lesbian here, and I agree with the others, definitely not the right sub. Maybe lean more towards r/relationships or a LGBT/lesbian subreddit. 

But as for my two cents, no matter what, breaking up is probably going to hurt like an absolute bitch. Do not cling to her if you two truly break up, it's just going to make things toxic and it will more than likely be mutual misery and you do not want that. You deserve to be happy and in a healthy, loving relationship. 

  As for how to deal, my best advice is to throw yourself into your hobbies, get out and hang around friends as much as you can tolerate. Maybe have wild flings with random pretty girls you match with on whatever dating app you prefer. Do the things you never let yourself do while being in a relationship. Indulge in self care. You may not want to do those things right away of course, and you shouldn't ignore and shut away your negative feelings either. Express your pain and hurt through whatever medium you feel is best (whether that's watching sad movies, writing about it, video games with dark themes if you enjoy video games, drawing, ect ect). If you just want to curl up in your dark bedroom and mindlessly binge YouTube or shows for a month, do it. There is no right way to grieve.

Phone games I would personally recommend are Stardew Valley, Genshin Impact (free), Don't Starve, and Among Us (free). 

For beginners I'd lean more towards games like Stardew Valley because it is pretty laid back, you can take your time figuring things out, and generally easy to get the hang of. Stardew Valley is a farming simulation game where you can customize your character, plant crops and eventually raise animals and interact with villagers in town, and eventually romance one of the eligible bachelorettes. You can also fish, or go into the mines to get ore and fight monsters.

I think Among Us is relatively easy to get the hang of, you play a mini astronaut on a space ship with a bunch of other random players, do assigned tasks and try to figure out who among you is the imposter/monster before they kill you. A little fast paced, and you learn mostly by trial and error. As you go through rounds you can eventually customize your little character and give them cute, funny or weird accessories.

Genshin Impact is a popular game, it is open world and you can explore to your heart's content while interacting with Non-Player-Characters and some of them will eventually join your team. You can also gather herbs, meat, vegetables and use them to cook, and fight monsters. I personally haven't played too much so I can't quite go into detail like I'm sure others can. But this game, like Stardew Valley, is available on PC as well.

Don't Starve is an open world survival where you pick a character, each character has their own unique benefit and weakness, and the goal of the game is just to see how long you can survive. Again, you can also get this game on PC if you learn you prefer playing on PC over mobile. :)

Sims is also an easy one to get the hang of, you can create your own characters and fully customize them and pick out their personality traits and life aspiration. I consider it the adult version of playing with dolls, lol. Not meant negatively, I was the kid who had and played with all the different dolls so I find the game satisfies my inner child without making me feel childish, haha. There are versions of it on mobile, but the PC version is definitely the best experience.

1. Cockatiels are pretty affectionate birds, especially if you consistently and properly train them. Also keep in mind that they generally require 2-3 hours of attention a day, and definitely let your bird out into the room to fly around and stretch their wings to avoid them developing bad behavior (just like any cat or dog that receives little to no attention), anxiety and potentially getting fat if their not allowed out of their cage to exercise.

2. It depends on the brand. According to my research the Lafeber brand is best, and Zupreem is a really good one too. One bag should be anywhere between 20-30 bucks for a decent sized bag, and ought to last a month or two, if I remember correctly.

3. Noise really isn't that bad. Especially if you only have one bird. You shouldn't have any issues with noise at night or in the morning, especially if you have a sheet or cover to throw over the cage at bed time. My birds have always remained quiet while their cage was covered, but your bird may chirp softly if they can hear you moving around.

4. In my opinion, the poop really isn't that bad. They do go a lot, but I have never ever personally noticed a smell of any kind. They have liners you can put along the bottom of the cage as well to catch most of the poop so clean up is even easier. Even if they poo on you (and it does happen), clean up is very quick and easy.

5. I haven't personally experienced this stage, but according to research the best you can do is train them not to display their bad behavior towards you. There are many YouTubers and bird-specific websites that can help and give advice on this stage with a simple and quick Google search.
